claims.text: The material under study is a Ti0.2Al0.2CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy multilayer coating on a titanium-alloy substrate.
High configurational entropy in Ti0.2Al0.2CoCrFeNi promotes formation of a stable oxide layer.
High configurational entropy in Ti0.2Al0.2CoCrFeNi promotes precipitation of secondary phases.
The secondary phases act as obstacles to dislocation glide.
Formation of the stable oxide layer contributes to increased resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation.
Obstruction of dislocation glide by secondary phases increases resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation.
The proposed test compares the creep behavior of the high-entropy-alloy coating with that of a conventional titanium-alloy coating under the same conditions.
A control group is proposed to address differences in substrate properties or coating-deposition methods.
The proposed test spans applied stresses of 200–800 MPa.
The high-entropy-alloy coating is predicted to have a longer creep lifetime than the conventional titanium-alloy coating.
The high-entropy-alloy coating is predicted to have a lower creep rate than the conventional titanium-alloy coating.
The claimed applicability boundary is 500–700 °C and 200–800 MPa.
Factors other than the proposed oxide and secondary-phase mechanism could influence the measured creep behavior.
Adding a control group can mitigate confounding from other factors affecting creep behavior.
Failure to observe both a longer creep lifetime and a lower creep rate relative to the conventional coating is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
